class.name: JarBodyLight
class.brief_description: Makes its JarCelestialBody a star that lights the scene.
class.description: Put it under a [JarCelestialBody] (the sun). Every frame it aims a [DirectionalLight3D] ([member JarBodyLayer.sun], else the first one in the scene) from the body's center at the camera, so the light comes from wherever the star is: as the universe turns around the anchor (a spinning planet, its orbit around the sun) the sun rises and sets. With [member physical_size] it also gives the light the star's real angular size, which sets the sun disk a sky shader draws from [code]LIGHT0_SIZE[/code] and the softness of shadows. Color, energy and shadows stay on the light. The light joins the group [code]"jar_body_light"[/code]: [JarVoxelUniverse] leaves it to the star (it does not turn it with the sky), and the other layers ([JarBodyWater], [JarBodyAtmosphere], [JarBodyClouds]) use it as their sun. The star itself is not drawn (it is usually far beyond the camera's far plane): the sky shows its disk. [method get_direction_at] and [method get_angular_diameter_at] give what effects such as a lens flare or an atmosphere need.

method.name: get_angular_diameter_at
method.description: The star's apparent diameter seen from [param global_position], in degrees (from its effective radius and distance).

method.name: get_direction_at
method.description: Unit direction from [param global_position] towards the star's center.

members.member: Sets the light's angular size ([member Light3D.light_angular_distance]) to the star's apparent size at the camera. Off: the light's own setting is kept.
